project: cellular-gaits — embodied escape (WP-D bundle for WP-E)
summary: Looming -> the real FlyWire connectome (LC4/LPLC2 -> DNp01 Giant Fiber) -> an embodied NeuroMechFly escape, precomputed for in-browser replay. Three conditions share env seed + warm-up so they diverge only at looming onset.

files.flee_left.mp4: left-threat escape clip (body bolts right, away) — birdseye
files.flee_right.mp4: right-threat escape clip (body turns left, away) — birdseye
files.flee_left_topdown.mp4: flee_left escape clip — topdown angle (WP3 alt)
files.flee_right_topdown.mp4: flee_right escape clip — topdown angle (WP3 alt)
files.walk_baseline_topdown.mp4: baseline walk clip — topdown angle (WP3 alt)

cameras.note: World-fixed legible cameras (R2-WP2): 'birdseye' (high 3/4 view) and 'topdown' (2D map) are bolted to the world, so the fly visibly travels across a static arena and the threat's approach reads (vs 'trackingcam', which recenters the fly and hides net displacement). Primary clips keep the canonical names; the second angle is suffixed (e.g. flee_left_topdown.mp4).

events.description: Per-condition moments the 2D/web view should mark, in trace.summary + trace.threat_track.
events.threat_onset_step: trace.threat_onset_step — step the looming threat launches (-1 for baseline).
events.pivot_step: trace.summary.pivot_step — first step after onset where |turn vs baseline| >= pivot_threshold_deg (10.0 deg): the decisive escape pivot (null for baseline / if never crossed).
events.threat_track: trace.threat_track — entry_xy (where the threat came from, its world pos at onset), aim_xy (lead point it flew at), and path_xy (per-step world x,y, null before onset) so the 2D view can draw the approach.

units.threat_xy: threat world x,y (body units; same frame as thorax_xy)

trace_fields.brain: per sync-window (window_step, t_s, loom_L/R, hz_L/R, dnp01_mean/L/R, drive, bearing_deg); baseline is flat zero
trace_fields.body: per control step (t_s, thorax_xy, thorax_z, yaw_deg)
trace_fields.summary: gf_peak_hz, drive_peak, displacement, heading_change_deg, turn_vs_baseline_deg {60ms,100ms,160ms,200ms} (the escape signature: unwrapped turn vs the no-threat baseline; left threat negative=bolts right, right threat positive=turns left), pivot_step / pivot_t_s / pivot_threshold_deg (R2-WP2 pivot event), threat_min_dist, threat_hit
trace_fields.threat_track: R2-WP2: onset_step, entry_xy, aim_xy, azimuth_deg, speed, radius, hit_radius, path_xy[] (per-step threat world xy, null pre-onset); null for baseline

caveats: Not a calibrated escape threshold: the isolated Giant Fiber saturates (no whole-brain inhibition). The claim is 'the real connectome routes a looming cue to an embodied escape', not selectivity.
The left-strong / right-weak escape asymmetry is the X-A body controller's, inherited and reported, not a new artifact.
Three interface mappings (loom->Hz, DNp01->drive, 15 ms sync) are hand-chosen knobs; one descending neuron stands in for the whole escape command; the looming front-end is a hand-built stand-in.
